chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia VerseEnd — Verse2 elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied. VerseEnd

Verse3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy has begotten us again unto a living hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead VerseEnd Verse4 to an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fades not away, reserved in Heaven for you VerseEnd Verse5 who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time, VerseEnd Verse6 wherein you greatly rejoice — though now for a season, if need be, you are afflicted through various temptations, VerseEnd Verse7 that the trial of your faith (being much more precious than of gold that perishes though it is tried with fire) might be found unto praise, and honor, and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse8 whom (having not seen) you love, in whom (though now you see him not, yet believing) you rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory, VerseEnd Verse9 receiving the object of your faith — even the salvation of your souls, VerseEnd Verse10 concerning which salvation the prophets (who prophesied of the grace bestowed upon you) inquired and searched diligently, VerseEnd Verse11 searching what time and what manner of salvation the spirit of Christ (which was in them) did signify when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glory which should follow, VerseEnd Verse12 unto whom it was revealed that not unto themselves but unto us they did minister the things which are now reported unto you by them who have preached the gospel unto you with the holy ghost sent down from Heaven, which things the angels desire to look into. VerseEnd

Verse13 Wherefore, gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse14 as obedient children — not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance. VerseEnd Verse15 But as he who has called you is holy, so be holy in all manner of conduct, VerseEnd Verse16 because it is written: Be holy, for I am holy. VerseEnd

Verse17 And if you call on the Father, who without respect of persons judges according to every man’s work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear, VerseEnd Verse18 forasmuch as you know that you were not redeemed with corruptible things (as silver and gold) from your vain conduct (received by tradition from your fathers) VerseEnd, Verse19 but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, VerseEnd Verse20 who truly was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you VerseEnd — Verse21 who by him do believe in God who raised him up from the dead and gave him glory, that your faith and hope might be in God. VerseEnd

Verse22 Seeing you have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that you love one another with a pure heart fervently, VerseEnd Verse23 being born again, not of corruptible seed but of incorruptible, by the word of God which lives and abides for ever. VerseEnd Verse24 For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withers and the flower thereof falls away, VerseEnd Verse25 but the word of the Lord endures for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached unto you. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 Wherefore, laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speaking, VerseEnd Verse2 as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that you may grow thereby, VerseEnd Verse3 if you have tasted that the Lord is gracious VerseEnd — Verse4 to whom coming, as unto a living stone (rejected indeed of men, but chosen of God and precious) VerseEnd Verse5 you also, as living stones, are built up a spiritual house, a holy Priesthood to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse6 Wherefore also, it is contained in the scripture: Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone (elect, precious) and he that believes on him shall not be confounded. VerseEnd

Verse7 Unto you therefore who believe, he is precious, but unto them who are disobedient, who stumble at the word through disobedience unto what they were appointed, VerseEnd Verse8 a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; for the stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. VerseEnd Verse9 But you are a chosen generation — a royal Priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people — that you should show forth the praises of him who has called you out of darkness into his marvelous light, VerseEnd Verse10 who in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God; who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy. VerseEnd

Verse11 Dearly beloved, I implore you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul, VerseEnd Verse12 having your conduct honest among the Gentiles — that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may, by your good works which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation. VerseEnd Verse13 Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake, whether it is to the king, as supreme, VerseEnd Verse14 or unto governors, as unto them that are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of them that do well; VerseEnd Verse15 for so is the will of God, that with well-doing you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men VerseEnd Verse16 as free, and not using your liberty for a cloak of maliciousness, but as the servants of God. VerseEnd Verse17 Honor all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honor the king. VerseEnd

Verse18 Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear — not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward. VerseEnd Verse19 For this is thankworthy: if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. VerseEnd Verse20 For what glory is it if, when you are buffeted for your faults, you shall take it patiently? But if, when you do well and suffer for it, you take it patiently, this is acceptable with God; VerseEnd Verse21 for even unto this were you called because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that you should follow his steps VerseEnd Verse22 who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth VerseEnd — Verse23 who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not, but committed himself to him that judges righteously; VerseEnd Verse24 who his own self bore our sins in his own body on the tree, that we being dead to sins should live unto righteousness; by whose stripes you were healed. VerseEnd Verse25 For you were as sheep going astray, but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 Likewise, you wives be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conduct of the wives, VerseEnd Verse2 while they behold your chaste conduct coupled with fear. VerseEnd Verse3 Let your adorning be not that outward adorning of plaiting the hair and wearing of gold, or putting on of apparel, VerseEnd Verse4 but let it be the hidden man of the heart — in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is (in the sight of God) of great VerseEnd Verse5 price. For after this manner, in old times, the holy women who trusted in God adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands, VerseEnd Verse6 even as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord — whose daughters you are, as long as you do well and are not afraid with any fear. VerseEnd

Verse7 Likewise, you husbands dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life, that your prayers be not hindered. VerseEnd

Verse8 Finally, be all of one mind, having compassion one for another. Love as brethren, be filled with pity, be courteous, VerseEnd Verse9 not rendering evil for evil or railing for railing, but contrariwise blessing, knowing that you are called unto this, that you should inherit a blessing. VerseEnd Verse10 For he that will love life and see good days, let him restrain his tongue from evil, and his lips, that they speak no guile. VerseEnd Verse11 Let him eschew evil and do good. Let him seek peace and pursue it. VerseEnd Verse12 For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous and his ears are open unto their prayers, but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil. VerseEnd

Verse13 And who is he that will harm you if you are followers of that which is good? VerseEnd Verse14 But if you suffer for righteousness’ sake, happy are you. And be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled, VerseEnd Verse15 but sanctify the Lord God in your hearts, and be ready always to give an answer with meekness and fear to every man that asks of you a reason for the hope that is in you, VerseEnd Verse16 having a good conscience, that whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed who falsely accuse your good conduct in Christ. VerseEnd

Verse17 For it is better, if the will of God should be so, that you suffer for well-doing than for evil doing, VerseEnd Verse18 for Christ also once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, being put to death in the flesh but quickened by the spirit, that he might bring us to God VerseEnd — Verse19 for which cause also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison, VerseEnd Verse20 some of whom were disobedient in the days of Noah while the long-suffering of God waited, while the ark was preparing, wherein few (that is, eight souls) were saved by water VerseEnd — Verse21 the like figure at which even baptism does also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse22 who is gone into Heaven and is on the right hand of God, angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 Forasmuch then as Christ has suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind, for you who have suffered in the flesh should cease from sin, VerseEnd Verse2 that you no longer — the rest of your time in the flesh — should live to the lusts of men, but to the will of God; VerseEnd Verse3 for the time past of life may suffice to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, when you walked in lasciviousness, lusts, excess of wine, revelings, banquetings, and abominable idolatries, VerseEnd Verse4 wherein they speak evil of you, thinking it strange that you run not with them to the same excess of riot, VerseEnd Verse5 who shall give account to him who is ready to judge the quick and the dead. VerseEnd Verse6 Because of this is the gospel preached to them who are dead — that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, but live in the spirit according to the will of God. VerseEnd

Verse7 But to you the end of all things is at hand; be therefore sober and watch unto prayer. VerseEnd Verse8 And above all things, have fervent charity among yourselves, for charity prevents a multitude of sins. VerseEnd Verse9 Use hospitality one to another without grudging. VerseEnd Verse10 As every man has received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the diverse grace of God. VerseEnd Verse11 If any man speak, let him speak as an oracle of God. If any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God gives, that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse12 Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you, VerseEnd Verse13 but rejoice inasmuch as you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, that when his glory shall be revealed, you may be glad also with exceeding joy. VerseEnd Verse14 If you should be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are you, for the spirit of glory and of God rests upon you (on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified) VerseEnd.

Verse15 But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters. VerseEnd Verse16 Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God on this behalf; VerseEnd Verse17 for the time has come that judgment must begin at the House of God, and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of those who obey not the gospel of God? VerseEnd Verse18 And if the righteous scarcely are saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear? VerseEnd Verse19 Wherefore, let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well-doing, as unto a faithful Creator. VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 The elders who are among you I exhort, who am also an elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed: VerseEnd Verse2 feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for base gain, but of a ready mind; VerseEnd Verse3 neither as being lords over God’s heritage, but by being examples to the flock. VerseEnd Verse4 And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, you shall receive a crown of glory that fades not away. VerseEnd

Verse5 Likewise, you younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another and be clothed with humility, for God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble. VerseEnd Verse6 Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time, VerseEnd Verse7 casting all your care upon him, for he cares for you. VerseEnd Verse8 Be sober, be vigilant, because your adversary, the Devil, as a roaring lion, walks about seeking whom he may devour VerseEnd — Verse9 whom resist, steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world. VerseEnd Verse10 But the God of all grace — who has called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a while, makes you perfect — establish, strengthen, settle you. VerseEnd Verse11 To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse12 By Silvanus, a faithful brother unto you as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting and testifying that this is the true grace of God wherein you stand. VerseEnd Verse13 They at Babylon, elected together with you, salute you, and so does Mark, my son. VerseEnd Verse14 Greet one another with a kiss of charity. Peace be with you all that are in Christ Jesus. Amen. VerseEnd
